### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 2 |
| **Summary** | This is a Penn State University Press (PSUP) publisher-wide policy, not JNS-specific (no separate JNS AI policy page found). PSUP requires full disclosure if AI was used in any way to complete a submitted article, distinguishing 'assistive AI' (editing/formatting/proofreading) from 'generative AI' (content creation/idea generation); editors and PSUP 'evaluate AI use to ensure it does not overstep ethical and professional publishing standards' — i.e. disclosure is mandatory and generative-AI use is subject to editorial discretion/approval rather than freely permitted. No mention of AI use in peer review specifically. |
| **Source URL** | https://www.psupress.org/journals/jnls_ethics_policies.html |

### Preprint Policy

> AI-research note (not broken down per-stage): Publisher-wide (PSUP) policy, not JNS-specific: accepted-article preprints/postprints may be deposited in institutional repositories or personal websites immediately upon publication with a link to the published version; commercial platforms (Academia.edu, ResearchGate) are explicitly excluded; separately, postprints become eligible for institutional-repository deposit after a one-year embargo. No explicit statement found on whether pre-submission preprinting (e.g. posting to a preprint server before/during review) is permitted — JNS does require exclusivity ('does not accept simultaneous submissions... must be the only journal or venue currently reviewing a submission'), which may bear on preprinting but is not stated as an explicit preprint rule.
> Source: https://www.psupress.org/journals/jnls_ethics_policies.html

| Dimension | Assessment |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Traditional English-language philosophical scholarship on Friedrich Nietzsche's work and thought: close textual/philological readings, historical-contextual studies, systematic argumentative philosophy papers, and comparative studies relating Nietzsche to other philosophers. 2024-2025 published titles include 'The Demon and His Message' (Robin Small), a piece on Plato and Nietzsche's epistemology (Mattia Riccardi), 'Plato and Nietzsche on the Ideal Soul' (Caroline Wall), '"The Realm of Our Invention": On the Role of Parody in Nietzsche's Thought' (David Sherman), 'Umwerthung in Action', and 'Tyranny, Freedom, and Moral Creativity in Nietzsche's "Middle Period"' plus book reviews (e.g. 'Nietzsche's Ethics', 'Conflict and Contest in Nietzsche's Philosophy'). No digital-humanities, empirical, or AI-related methodology found in recent tables of contents.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** close textual/philological reading of Nietzsche's works, historical-contextual scholarship using primary/archival resources, systematic philosophical argumentation, comparative philosophy (Nietzsche in relation to other philosophers, e.g. Plato), engagement with Nietzsche's contemporary philosophical relevance
